name: review-desk
goal: Build the logic behind CrossTalk's review desk: the INI index that queues items for a human, the rule that an approval needs no explanation while a rejection or question does, and the anchors that keep a note attached to the right lines of a file even after the file changes. Claude builds the Windows GUI on top of these three modules.

tasks.instructions: This enforces Kris's review rule: an approval needs no explanation, a rejection or a question does. Nothing here touches a file or a clock.
tasks.test_instructions: Prove that an approval with no note is accepted and a rejection with no note is not, and that a defer never wakes the agent.

tasks.instructions: The index is a file a human may open in Notepad, so the round trip matters more than cleverness. merge must never overwrite a decision a human already made.
tasks.test_instructions: Include a note containing a newline, an = sign and a semicolon, and prove merge leaves a decided item completely alone.

tasks.instructions: A note pinned to a line must survive the file changing, or say plainly that it cannot. Matching is exact, including indentation: a comment must never drift onto code that merely resembles the code it was written about.
tasks.test_instructions: Cover all four relocate outcomes - unchanged, moved, ambiguous, stale - and prove that a change in indentation makes an anchor stale rather than moved.
